results.result: yoU-Net, a user-friendly U-Net-based deep learning framework, accurately binarizes images of cardiac sarcomeres and their precursors stained with α-actinin-2, titin, and myomesin after training with 1000 steps for α-actinin-2, 125 epochs for titin, and 50 epochs for myomesin.
results.evaluation: Claims C49-C50 describe yoU-Net's development and capabilities, while C59-C61 detail the training procedure and performance for α-actinin-2 (achieving 97.1% validation metric). Claims C106 and C123 demonstrate successful application to titin (60.4% validation, underestimated due to sparse labeling) and myomesin (84.7% validation) respectively. The tool successfully addresses the binarization bottleneck described in C33-C36.

results.result: sarcApp automatically quantifies sarcomere structures in real space, classifying α-actinin-2 structures as Z-Lines (>1.4 µm) or Z-Bodies (≤1.4 µm), assigning them to myofibrils or MSFs based on geometric criteria, and producing 33 measurements per cell and 24 per myofibril including titin doublets/rings and myomesin M-Lines.
results.evaluation: Claims C9-C14 and C51 establish sarcApp's core functionality. Claims C62-C84 detail the classification algorithms and criteria for α-actinin-2 structures with customizable parameters (C64, C79). Claims C107-C112 describe titin analysis capabilities (doublet threshold 1.7 µm based on C107-C108), and C124-C127 detail myomesin M-Line quantification. The comprehensive output metrics (C72-C76) are well-documented and address the manual quantification bottleneck (C36).

results.result: Blebbistatin treatment (50-100 µM) dose-dependently inhibits sarcomere assembly in hiCMs, reducing myofibrils per cell, Z-Lines per cell, myofibril persistence length, Z-Line length, and causing random myofibril orientation, as validated by sarcApp quantification and platinum-replica EM.
results.evaluation: Claims C85-C86 establish Blebbistatin as a validated inhibitor. Claims C87-C89 describe the experimental system. Claims C91-C101 present quantitative findings from sarcApp analysis (Figures 3C-H) showing significant dose-dependent effects with appropriate statistical testing (p-values reported). Platinum-replica EM (C92-C93, Figure 3B) provides orthogonal validation. Claim C102 correctly notes consistency with prior literature. The validation successfully demonstrates sarcApp's functionality.

results.result: Blebbistatin treatment affects titin doublet assembly (fewer and shorter doublets at 100 µM) and ring morphology (more rounded, decreased aspect ratio) while maintaining myofibril periodicity, but causes random myofibril orientation relative to cell edge.
results.evaluation: Claims C113-C118 present sarcApp quantification of titin structures under Blebbistatin treatment (Figure 5B-G). The findings show no effect on myofibril number (C113) but significant effects on doublet number/length (C114-C115) and ring aspect ratio (C117) with appropriate statistical testing. Claim C118 demonstrates consistency with α-actinin-2 findings. Claim C119 provides a reasonable summary interpretation. The data suggest titin structures can form periodic arrangements despite myosin II inhibition.

results.result: Blebbistatin treatment reduces M-Line assembly in hiCMs, resulting in fewer myofibrils per cell, fewer M-Lines per cell, shortened M-Line length, and disorganized myofibril orientation relative to cell edge as measured by myomesin staining.
results.evaluation: Claims C128-C132 present sarcApp quantification of myomesin-stained M-Lines under Blebbistatin treatment (Figure 6E-I). Visual observations (C128) are confirmed by quantitative analysis showing significant reductions in myofibril number (C129), M-Line number (C130), and M-Line length (C131) with appropriate statistical testing (p-values reported). Claim C132 demonstrates disorganized orientation consistent with Z-Line findings. The data validate sarcApp's M-Line quantification capability.

results.result: α myosin II (MYH6) knockdown does not alter Z-Line, titin doublet, or M-Line length in hiCMs, though one siRNA increased Z-Line numbers, suggesting α myosin II is not strictly required for Z- or M-Line assembly.
results.evaluation: Claims C137-C141 present sarcApp quantification following MYH6 knockdown (Figure 7C-G). Western blot validation (Figure 7B) confirms knockdown. The data show no significant effects on structure lengths (C138-C140) across multiple sarcomere components, with one siRNA showing increased Z-Line number (C141). Claim C147 provides a reasonable conclusion supported by the data and consistent with prior work in Xenopus (C149). The multi-component analysis demonstrates the value of comprehensive sarcomere assessment.

results.result: β myosin II (MYH7) knockdown results in more abundant but shorter Z-Lines and significantly shorter M-Lines without affecting titin doublet length, suggesting β myosin II is not strictly required for assembly but influences Z-Line concatenation and M-Line maturation.
results.evaluation: Claims C142-C146 present sarcApp quantification following MYH7 knockdown (Figure 7H-M). Western blot validation (Figure 7H) confirms knockdown. The data show significant increases in Z-Line number (C143) with decreased length (C144), no effect on titin doublets (C145), but shortened M-Lines (C146) with appropriate statistical testing. Claims C147-C148 provide reasonable conclusions distinguishing β myosin II's role in concatenation from strict requirement for assembly. This demonstrates differential effects on Z-Lines versus M-Lines.

results.result: Myomesin knockdown does not affect Z-Line or titin doublet assembly but increases titin precursor rings, reduces A-band organization, and shortens β myosin II stacks, suggesting myomesin regulates A-band/M-Line assembly but not Z-Line assembly, indicating decoupled regulatory mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C150-C156 present sarcApp quantification following myomesin knockdown (Figure 8A-G) with western blot validation (Figure 8B). The data show no effect on Z-Line number (C151) or titin doublets (C154-C155), but increased titin rings (C156) and one siRNA showing decreased Z-Line length (C153). Claims C157-C158 show reduced A-band organization and shorter myosin stacks (Figure 8H-I). Claims C159-C160 provide well-supported conclusions about decoupled Z-Line and M-Line assembly mechanisms, which is a key finding of the study.

results.result: Perturbations affect Z-Lines and M-Lines differently (β myosin II and myomesin knockdowns show differential effects), suggesting independent regulation during sarcomere assembly and emphasizing the need for multi-component analysis rather than using Z-Lines alone as a proxy for sarcomere status.
results.evaluation: Claims C16-C17 and C52 state the main finding that Z-Lines and M-Lines respond differently to perturbations. This is supported by the differential effects observed in β myosin II knockdown (C143-C146) and myomesin knockdown (C151-C159). Claims C53-C54 and C160 interpret these findings as evidence for modular/decoupled assembly. Claims C161-C162 provide important methodological recommendations. The conclusion is well-supported by the comprehensive multi-component analysis throughout the study.

results.result: Myofibril orientation analysis reveals that control hiCMs assemble myofibrils approximately parallel to the cell edge, while Blebbistatin treatment causes random orientation, suggesting disrupted organizational mechanisms.
results.evaluation: Claims C77 and C99 establish baseline myofibril orientation in control cells (parallel to edge). Claims C100-C101 show Blebbistatin-induced random orientation for α-actinin-2-labeled myofibrils (Figure 3H). Claim C118 demonstrates consistency with titin-labeled myofibrils (Figure 5G), and C132 shows the same for myomesin-labeled myofibrils (Figure 6I). The consistent findings across multiple markers strengthen the conclusion about disrupted organization. This demonstrates sarcApp's novel orientation quantification capability (C74-C75).

results.result: Titin localizes to both MSFs and sarcomeres in hiCMs, forming ringlike structures around Z-Bodies with the N-terminus toward the center and C-terminus radially outward, and the I-Band signal wraps around Z-Line tips.
results.evaluation: Claims C103-C104 describe titin localization patterns observed in images (Figure 4A). Claim C105 proposes a model for titin orientation based on antibody localization and known binding properties (supported by citations), but this is presented as an inference rather than direct experimental evidence. Claim C109 describes an additional observation. While the observations are documented, the mechanistic model for titin orientation (C105) requires additional validation beyond antibody localization patterns and literature knowledge.

results.result: The study used fixed-cell immunofluorescence with unbiased cell selection (DAPI-based) to capture biological variability, and sarcApp was designed for 2D quantification based on prior findings that sarcomeres assemble on the dorsal surface within a 2D plane for up to 48 hours.
results.evaluation: Claims C163-C164 describe the methodology and bias minimization approach. Claim C165 asserts representativeness based on the unbiased selection, which is reasonable but somewhat overstated ("fully captures" is strong language). Claims C168-C169 explain the 2D design choice based on prior published work (citations provided). The methodological choices are well-justified, though the claim about fully capturing variability (C165) is more of an inference than a demonstrated fact.

results.result: Background knowledge claims establish that sarcomeres are the basic contractile units in cardiac muscle, their alignment is critical for function and disease, α-actinin-2 marks Z-Lines, sarcomere assembly models exist but are limited by lack of high-throughput analysis tools, and hiCMs provide a tractable model system.
results.evaluation: These claims (C1-C6, C18-C32, C42-C43, C120, C133-C134, C136) represent established knowledge supported by appropriate citations throughout. They provide necessary context for the study but are not novel findings. The claims about field limitations (C7-C8, C30, C33-C36, C47-C48) motivate the tool development. All background claims are appropriately supported by literature citations or represent standard knowledge in the field.

results.result: The authors speculate that sarcApp and yoU-Net will facilitate future high-throughput studies, enable broader researcher access to cardiac cell biology, and could be extended to live-cell and 3D analysis, though these represent future goals rather than current capabilities.
results.evaluation: Claims C55, C166-C167, C170, C172-C174 represent speculations about future impact and development directions. While the tools' potential is reasonable given their demonstrated capabilities, these are forward-looking statements rather than current results. Claims C171 summarizes what the tools currently provide (supported), but the anticipated applications (C172) and future developments (C166-C167, C170) are speculative. The open-source availability supports potential for community adoption (C173-C174).

results.result: The yoU-Net deep learning tool can accurately binarize immunofluorescence images of sarcomeric proteins (α-actinin-2, titin, myomesin) in hiCMs, overcoming limitations of classical intensity-based methods like Otsu thresholding. The trained U-Net produces high-fidelity binaries resistant to pixel intensity artifacts and can accurately separate individual Z-Bodies.
results.evaluation: Reviewers explicitly affirm the tool's utility and accuracy. One reviewer states the binarization tool 'appears promising' and notes 'example from one image suggests their binarization tool outperforms Otsu thresholding binarization.' Another reviewer confirms 'the work is solid, and the methods, data and analyses broadly support the claims.' The tool's performance is accepted without challenge.

results.result: sarcApp is an automated image analysis software that classifies and quantifies sarcomeric structures (Z-Lines, Z-Bodies, M-Lines, titin doublets/rings) in real space, assigning them to myofibrils or MSFs, and produces 33 measurements per cell and 24 per myofibril across multiple sarcomeric proteins.
results.evaluation: Reviewers consistently affirm sarcApp's capabilities. One states 'the authors developed and made publicly available an excellent software tool that will be very useful for labs that are interested in studying sarcomere assembly. Multiple features that are difficult to measure or count manually can be automatically measured by the software quickly and accurately.' Another notes the tool 'will be relevant to biologists working on and interested in obtaining quantitative information on sarcomere structure, function and development.'

results.result: Blebbistatin treatment of hiCMs results in reduced and disorganized sarcomere assembly, with fewer myofibrils, fewer Z-Lines, decreased myofibril persistence length, decreased Z-Line length, and more randomly oriented myofibrils compared to controls, as quantified by sarcApp.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these validation results without challenge. One reviewer explicitly states 'the sarcApp tool could capture changes in multiple features such as fewer myofibrils, fewer Z-Lines, decreased myofibril persistence, decreased Z-Line length and altered myofibril orientation in the Blebbistatin treated cells.' The data are described as 'consistent with a wide range of previous studies' and the validation is treated as successful.

results.result: Titin-based quantification with sarcApp reveals that Blebbistatin treatment results in fewer and shorter titin doublets, more rounded titin precursor rings, and disarrayed myofibril orientation, while the number of myofibrils and titin rings remains unchanged.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these titin-specific findings. The tool's ability to quantify titin structures is accepted as part of the overall validation, with one reviewer noting 'with some changes the tool was also shown to quantify sarcomeres in titin and myomesin stained cardiomyocytes.' The differential effects on different sarcomeric components are implicitly accepted.

results.result: Blebbistatin treatment affects M-Lines as measured by myomesin staining, resulting in fewer myofibrils, fewer M-Lines, shortened M-Line length, and disorganized myofibril orientation relative to the cell edge.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept the M-Line quantification results without objection. One reviewer explicitly acknowledges that the tool 'was also shown to quantify sarcomeres in titin and myomesin stained cardiomyocytes.' The M-Line findings are treated as part of the successful validation of sarcApp's multi-component analysis capabilities.

results.result: Perturbations to sarcomere assembly (myosin knockdowns, myomesin knockdown) affect Z-Lines and M-Lines differently, suggesting that Z-Line and M-Line/A-band assembly are decoupled and regulated by at least partially independent mechanisms during sarcomere assembly in hiCMs.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept this key biological conclusion. One reviewer summarizes: 'The analysis indicates that neither MYH6 nor MYH7 knockdown perturbed the assembly of Z- or M-lines, and that knockdown of MYOM perturbed the A-band/M-Line but not the Z-Line assembly according to features captured by the sarcApp tool.' Another states the authors 'demonstrated that different muscle myosins participate in sarcomere assembly in different manners.' The conclusion about independent regulation is not challenged.

results.result: α myosin II (MYH6) knockdown does not alter the length of α-actinin-2 Z-lines, titin doublets, or M-lines, though one siRNA resulted in increased numbers of Z-lines.
results.evaluation: Reviewers do not challenge these findings. The results are accepted as part of the demonstration that 'neither MYH6 nor MYH7 knockdown perturbed the assembly of Z- or M-lines' as one reviewer notes. The data support the broader conclusion about independent regulation of sarcomeric components.

results.result: β myosin II (MYH7) knockdown results in more abundant but shorter Z-lines, no change in titin doublet lengths, and significantly shorter M-lines compared to controls.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings without objection. The differential effects on Z-lines versus M-lines are treated as supporting evidence for the main conclusion about modular sarcomere assembly. One reviewer acknowledges the authors 'demonstrated that different muscle myosins participate in sarcomere assembly in different manners.'

results.result: Myomesin knockdown does not affect Z-Line assembly (no difference in Z-Lines per cell) but results in less organized A-bands with shorter β myosin II stacks and increased numbers of titin precursor rings, suggesting myomesin regulates A-band/M-Line assembly but not Z-Line assembly.
results.evaluation: Reviewers accept these findings as supporting the main biological conclusion. One reviewer explicitly states 'knockdown of MYOM perturbed the A-band/M-Line but not the Z-Line assembly according to features captured by the sarcApp tool.' The differential effects are treated as key evidence for independent regulation of sarcomeric components.

results.result: U-Net offers advantages of superior accuracy and speed compared to manual binarization, but requires users with advanced mathematical background, machine learning experience, and coding proficiency.
results.evaluation: Reviewers acknowledge the tool's advantages but raise concerns about accessibility and robustness. One reviewer notes 'the binarization tool which is tailored to sarcomere image binarization appears promising but was not systematically compared with existing approaches.' Another questions 'how robust is the tool?' noting it was tested only on 'one type of cardiomyocytes (hiCMs) taken from one lab using' specific microscopy systems, raising concerns about generalizability.

results.result: Current frequency space methods for sarcomere quantification yield no information about Z-Lines in real space (number, size, spacing, organization within myofibrils), about sarcomere precursors, or about sarcomeric components other than Z-Lines, and it is unclear how Z-Line assembly relates spatially or temporally to other sarcomere components.
results.evaluation: One reviewer expresses surprise that 'there is no reference in the manuscript to SarcTrack, published by Toepfer and colleagues in 2019 (PMID 30700234), which has exactly the same purpose,' suggesting the authors may have overstated the limitations of existing methods. The reviewer notes 'the advantage of the image analysis software presented in the current manuscript appears to me to be that it can cover both mature sarcomeres and nascent sarcomeres in premyofibrils effectively,' implying existing tools may address some of the claimed gaps.

comparisons.comparison: Both evaluations support the yoU-Net binarization tool's development and performance (C49-C50, C60-C61, C106, C123). OpenEval provides detailed validation metrics (97.1% for α-actinin-2, 60.4% for titin, 84.7% for myomesin), while peer reviewers affirm the tool 'appears promising' and 'outperforms Otsu thresholding.' Both agree the tool successfully addresses the binarization bottleneck.

Both evaluations strongly support sarcApp's comprehensive functionality (C9-C14, C51, C65-C67, C72-C73, C110-C111, C124, C126). OpenEval details the classification algorithms and customizable parameters, while peer reviewers describe it as 'an excellent software tool' that can 'automatically measure' multiple features 'quickly and accurately.' Both recognize the tool's value for multi-component sarcomere analysis.

Both evaluations support the Blebbistatin validation results (C91-C98, C100, C102). OpenEval emphasizes quantitative findings with statistical testing and orthogonal EM validation, while peer reviewers accept that 'sarcApp tool could capture changes in multiple features' and note consistency with previous studies. Both treat the validation as successful demonstration of sarcApp's functionality.

Both evaluations support the titin-specific Blebbistatin findings (C113-C119). OpenEval details the quantitative effects on doublet number/length and ring aspect ratio with statistical testing, while peer reviewers accept the tool's ability to 'quantify sarcomeres in titin and myomesin stained cardiomyocytes' without challenge. Both recognize differential effects across sarcomeric components.

Perfect agreement on myomesin M-Line quantification under Blebbistatin treatment (C128-C132). OpenEval provides detailed statistical analysis of reductions in myofibril number, M-Line number/length, and disorganized orientation. Peer reviewers accept these results as part of successful validation of sarcApp's multi-component analysis capabilities without objection.

Both evaluations support MYH6 knockdown findings (C138-C141). OpenEval notes no significant effects on structure lengths with one siRNA showing increased Z-Line number, while peer reviewers accept that 'neither MYH6 nor MYH7 knockdown perturbed the assembly of Z- or M-lines.' Both treat these results as supporting the broader conclusion about independent regulation.

Both evaluations support MYH7 knockdown findings (C143-C146). OpenEval details significant increases in Z-Line number with decreased length, no effect on titin doublets, but shortened M-Lines. Peer reviewers accept these differential effects as demonstrating 'different muscle myosins participate in sarcomere assembly in different manners.' Both recognize the distinction between β myosin II's roles.

Both evaluations support myomesin knockdown findings (C151-C158). OpenEval details no effect on Z-Line number or titin doublets but increased titin rings and reduced A-band organization. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'knockdown of MYOM perturbed the A-band/M-Line but not the Z-Line assembly.' Both treat these as key evidence for decoupled assembly mechanisms.

Both evaluations support the main biological conclusion about modular/decoupled sarcomere assembly (C16-C17, C52, C54, C147, C160). OpenEval emphasizes differential responses across perturbations and provides methodological recommendations. Peer reviewers accept that the analysis 'indicates that neither MYH6 nor MYH7 knockdown perturbed the assembly of Z- or M-lines' and acknowledge independent regulation without challenge.

OpenEval identifies consistent orientation findings across multiple markers (C77, C99-C101, C118, C132) as demonstrating sarcApp's novel orientation quantification capability. No corresponding peer review evaluation specifically addresses this cross-marker consistency pattern, though individual results are accepted in other concordance records.

OpenEval rates titin localization observations and orientation model (C103-C105, C109) as UNCERTAIN, noting the mechanistic model is an inference requiring additional validation beyond antibody localization. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these titin orientation claims.

OpenEval supports the methodology and bias minimization approach (C163-C165, C168-C169) as well-justified, though notes 'fully captures' variability is somewhat overstated. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these methodological design claims.

OpenEval supports extensive background and context claims (C1-C6, C18-C32, C42-C43, C120, C133-C134, C136) as established knowledge with appropriate citations. Peer reviewers do not systematically evaluate these background claims, though R11 questions whether field limitations were overstated regarding existing tools.

OpenEval rates future impact and development claims (C55, C166-C167, C170-C174) as UNCERTAIN, noting these are forward-looking speculations rather than current results. Peer reviewers do not specifically evaluate these future-oriented claims.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation of tool advantages (C40-C41), raising concerns about accessibility, robustness, and generalizability beyond one cell type and microscopy system. They note the binarization tool 'was not systematically compared with existing approaches.' OpenEval does not have a corresponding evaluation specifically addressing these limitation claims.

Peer reviewers express UNCERTAIN evaluation of claims about existing method limitations (C47-C48), noting surprise at no reference to SarcTrack (2019) which has 'exactly the same purpose,' suggesting authors may have overstated gaps in existing tools. OpenEval includes these claims in R13 as supported background but does not separately evaluate the characterization of field limitations.
